title: The Holy Trinity
definition: God is one in essence and three in Persons: the Father, the Son, and the Holy Spirit. The three share one undivided divine nature, equal in glory and co-eternal in majesty, yet they are not three gods but one God. The Father is unbegotten, the Son is eternally begotten of the Father, and the Spirit eternally proceeds from the Father. This is the God the Orthodox Church worships and confesses in the Creed.
tradition: The Church's confession of the Trinity was forged against the Arian denial that the Son is truly God. The First Ecumenical Council at Nicaea (325) declared the Son to be 'of one essence' (homoousios) with the Father, and the Second at Constantinople (381) completed the confession of the Spirit's deity. The fathers cited here stand on both sides of that crisis.
